item.title: Large Format Portraits — An analogue experience for everyone
item.description:
There was a moment in the workshop, while we were developing the first portrait on paper, when someone said: “Wait — you can actually see the face.” Yes. The face of the person standing in front of you, appearing in black and white inside a tray. It’s wonderful the first time. The fifth time too.

How it went

At Cameras & Films we brought our large format camera — the Woody, an old 4×5" wooden camera — and spent the morning making portraits. The setup: part of the group posed, the other part photographed, and we rotated.

item.title: Rain, Zenits and a serious passion for analogue photography
item.description:
On 1 February, at Cameras & Films (formerly Lomography Store Barcelona), we ran one of our most beloved workshops: film developing in black and white.

Despite the day starting with a few hiccups, it ended up being a rich, rewarding experience.

The day

Rain arrived from the morning, which forced us to rethink some parts of the workshop on the fly. Light was in short supply, and I myself — yes, a little unprepared — hadn’t come ready enough for such a wet day.

item.title: Large Format Portraits at Cameras & Films — August 2024
item.description:
Bring Arezzo — said the workshop announcement — and come learn to load, focus and shoot our old large format Woody camera.

The idea: we combine the experience of operating a large format camera with portrait technique. You arrive as a photographer and leave having also been a model. Or the other way round.

Best of all: we developed the portraits immediately in the shop’s darkroom. All the magic of analogue photography, live.

item.title: Developing workshop at Cameras & Films — July 2024
item.description:
Another black-and-white developing workshop at Cameras & Films (formerly Lomography Embassy Barcelona).

Learning to develop a roll of film is one of those things that, once you’ve done it, you can’t stop. Loading the film into the tank in the dark, measuring the chemicals, checking the temperature, agitating, waiting. And when you open the tank and see there’s an image… there’s nothing quite like it.
